evidence.mechanism: shot-08s: a patch of about 60 ochre and rust triangles fills the frame from apex to base, each tile split by graphite edge lines; by shot-20s the same growth yields a few hundred smaller tiles.
evidence.ambition: shot-08s: one flat 2D layer of tiles plus a two-bar legend, with no lighting, material or extra layers; by shot-20s density rises sharply, but the bytes buy one generator and little rendering depth.
evidence.craft: shot-02s: crisp graphite edges on flat ochre and rust fills over a cream ground, and the palette matches the brief; the seed cluster sits right of centre and the left legend bars are tiny. By shot-20s no seams are visible.
evidence.distinctness: shot-02s: kite and dart triangles in cream, ochre and rust, with no noise fill, birds or plasma; by shot-20s tile clusters meet at star-like vertices, a non-periodic structure none of the four anchors show.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: a sparse cluster sits off-centre with large empty areas; by shot-20s the frame fills and resolves, but the left legend bars stay the same height at all three times, so the count shift never shows.

pairwise_justification: No median archive exists yet, so the pairwise check defaults to true by rule.

critique.change: Drive the left legend bars from the live kite and dart counts. They stay the same height at shot-02s, shot-08s and shot-20s, so the count lock never shows. Let them trade shares as each generation adds tiles.

Centre the seed cluster at shot-02s, where it sits right of centre with a large empty field. Add the brief's push-in on the newest shell and pull-back to the whole patch, so the three shots differ in scale.
Tint each new generation a distinct ochre and let older shells fade to pale ochre, as the brief describes. Right now the flat fills show one layer, so the shell growth reads as one mass.
